Coating Challenges in Machine Shops

Machined parts are hard to coat well because the finish must cover outer surfaces without entering threads, bores or sealing faces. The main challenges are cutting oil residue, tight tolerances, sharp edges and small batches that still need a fast, repeatable turnaround.

Cutting oil and coolant soak into machined surfaces and show up later as craters or poor adhesion, so degreasing has to be thorough. Sharp edges pull powder thin, and film that lands inside threads or bearing bores can stop a fit. Powder coating for machine shop parts works when masking, cleaning and film control are planned before the first part goes into the oven.

Batch size adds pressure. A shop may send twenty brackets today and fifty housings next week, each with different masking needs. Machine shop powder coating therefore depends on written masking notes and a colour code on file, so batch consistency holds from one run to the next. Powder coating for machine shops has to solve all of this at once.

Mixed metals complicate the schedule further. Aluminum, steel and stainless parts need different cleaning, and small precision pieces cure faster than heavy bases. A finisher offering real powder coating for machine shop parts plans each metal and each size separately, so one oven load never compromises another.
Parts and Metals We Coat for Machine Shops

We coat CNC machined parts in steel, aluminum and stainless steel, including housings, brackets, fixtures and jigs, shafts, plates and covers. Parts range from small-part batches to larger machined bases within our 6,000 lb capacity.

Aluminum housings and covers are cleaned for good adhesion and are often finished in matte black or a custom RAL colour. Steel brackets and plates take well to blasting and phosphate pre-treatment when they carry rust or heat scale. Our powder coating for machined parts covers the following work:

blocks.text: Powder coating for CNC parts follows a written plan for every part: which surfaces are coated, which stay bare and how each piece hangs in the oven. Hanging points are chosen on non-critical areas, so racks never mark a finished face. Our [capabilities page](/capabilities) lists current size and weight limits, so you can check a part before sending it.

Geometry shapes the plan too. Blind holes, deep pockets and tight internal corners are hard for powder to reach, so we review them before racking. Stainless parts get a different cleaning routine from carbon steel. Machine shop powder coating also considers weight: small components can share a rack, while heavy plates hang alone, which keeps cure even across the load.
Finishes and Specs for Machined Parts

Most machine shop powder coating uses a thermoset powder in polyester, epoxy or hybrid, applied by electrostatic spray and cured in the oven at roughly 180–200 °C. We match RAL colour codes and offer matte, gloss, satin and textured finishes.

Choosing the right finish is part of powder coating for machine shops done well, and film thickness matters more on machined work than on most fabrications. Even a thin coating can affect a fit, so we agree a target at quote and flag any feature that cannot take a coating. Matte black is a popular choice for housings and covers because it hides tool marks and light handling wear.

Colour is usually simple on machine shop work. Black, grey and safety colours suit guards and fixtures, while customer-branded equipment calls for an exact RAL match. We record the colour code and powder on every order, so later jobs match. Powder coating for machinists who supply branded equipment benefits most from that record.

Quality is checked, not assumed. Coating thickness is measured with a calibrated gauge following ASTM D7091, adhesion can be tested to ASTM D3359, and test reports are available on request. Our quality steps for powder coating for machine shop parts are documented with the Absolute Bureau of Certification, so your own customer can ask for proof.

Tight tolerances get a documented plan. Tell us which fits, threads and mating surfaces are critical, and we will mark them on the work order before coating starts. Precision masking is part of every quote, not an extra.
How We Work With Machine Shops

Our machine shop powder coating process runs from quote to delivery in a fixed sequence: inspection, degreasing, masking, coating, curing, quality check and packaging. Standard orders leave in 48 hours, and our shop is open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.

items: Send drawings with part counts, metal, finish and the surfaces that must stay bare.
We inspect the parts and confirm masking, powder and delivery timing in writing.
Parts are degreased, cleaned and, where needed, pre-treated.
Threads, bores and faces are masked with silicone plugs and masking tape.
Powder is applied by electrostatic spray and cured in the oven.
Each batch is inspected and packed to protect the finish, then released for pickup and delivery.

Machine Shop Coating FAQs

Short answer: powder coating for machine shops works best when masking, film thickness and timing are agreed before parts arrive. These answers cover threads, tolerances, batch sizes and quotes for machined work.

blocks.q: Can you keep threaded holes and bores free of powder?
blocks.a: Yes. Good powder coating for machinists plugs threaded holes and masks bores, journals and sealing faces before coating. Mark the critical features on your drawing, and we record them with your order. Very fine threads are best discussed at quote.

blocks.q: Will powder coating affect my tolerances?
blocks.a: In CNC powder coating, the powder adds film, so fit-critical surfaces should be masked or left bare. For features that can take a coating, we agree a target thickness at quote and measure it after curing.

Yes. For powder coating for machined parts, we coat small batches as well as larger runs, and we can combine different parts in one order when the powder and colour match. Tell us the quantities and finish at quote.

blocks.q: How fast can machine shops get parts back?
blocks.a: Standard orders are returned in 48 hours. Heavy sandblasting, special colours and large parts can take longer, and we confirm the timing in writing before work starts.

blocks.q: What should I send for a quote?
blocks.a: Send a drawing or photos, the metal, quantities, finish and any surfaces that must stay bare. A sample part helps with complex masking, and our quote form accepts photo uploads.

blocks.q: Do you coat stainless steel and aluminum parts?
blocks.a: Yes. Both are routine for machine shops, and each metal gets its own cleaning and cure plan. List the metal for every part when you request a quote, so powder coating for machine shops can be scheduled without guesswork.
